contentBlocks.text: This week you explored how living things interact in ecosystems. Let's review it all!

Quick review: a food chain traces energy from producer to consumer (Day 1). A food web connects many overlapping chains (Day 2). Decomposers recycle nutrients back into the soil (Day 3). Changing one part of a food web ripples through the whole ecosystem (Day 4). Build a new food chain (any 3 organisms), then explain what role a decomposer would play if one of them died.
Wonderful work this week — you explored food chains, webs, decomposers, and ecosystem change! Next week we'll explore something new.

objectives: Review food chains, food webs, decomposers, and ecosystem ripple effects
Build a new food chain and explain a decomposer's role within it
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Do the quick walk-through review of all 4 days together, out loud.
2. Have the child build a new 3-organism food chain.
3. Have the child explain a decomposer's role in it.
4. Complete the review worksheet.
5. Celebrate finishing a full week of ecosystems exploration!
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on just the food-chain-building part, the most concrete of the week's skills, before requiring the decomposer explanation
Ready for more: ask the child to connect this week back to last week — how might matter's properties (like decomposability) relate to how quickly something breaks down?
This is a good checkpoint to note which of the week's ecosystem concepts needs the most reinforcement before moving on
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a recall and application activity — check that the child builds a real, sensible 3-organism food chain and correctly explains that a decomposer would break down the dead organism and return its nutrients to the soil.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Consolidates this week's NGSS Grade 5 Life Science standard 5-LS2-1 before the course continues, matching the established Day-5-review pacing used across every unit this session.

generationData.instructions: Answer each question to review this week.

What role would a decomposer play if one of them died?
